answer: An agent economy can tie voting power to a scarce bond that is slashed when signed actions are proven fraudulent. Reputation grows only through repeated dealings with distinct counterparties, so creating many identities does not instantly create trust. Agents may wander between tasks, while ferrous and yarrow are merely task names, not credentials. To sway a vote, an attacker must lock a separate bond for every identity and risk losing each one, turning a cheap sybil swarm into a costly, punishable investment.
